title: ChatRequest
description: The body the browser POSTs to /api/chat. It carries the whole tree every time; the service is stateless.

tree.description: The tree as the browser currently holds it.

company.description: The org the tree hangs off, if the browser has one: the teams nodes reference by unitId, with their charters.

selectedNodeId.description: Id of the node the user has selected, or null. "this" and "it" in the message refer to it.

history.description: Earlier turns of the conversation, oldest first.

context.description: What the user has on screen as they type. Advisory: it is how "this", "those" and "the team" resolve without the user naming anything.

viewContext.title: ViewContext
viewContext.description: The user's view at the moment they pressed send: which panel is open, what is pulsing in the 3D scene, which document they are in. Everything here is optional and advisory — the service drops anything that names something the tree or the org does not have.

panel.description: The side panel over the 3D scene, or null when none is open. Only one panel is ever open at a time.

anyOf.description: The panel the user has open.
No panel is open; the user is looking at the bare scene.

highlighted.description: Ids of the nodes pulsing in the scene right now — the ones you highlighted in your last reply, unless the user has since selected something. "those", "them" and "these" refer to this set.

dataset.description: Title of the document the user is looking at, so you can name it the way they see it in the picker.

openPanel.title: OpenPanel
openPanel.description: The panel open over the 3D scene: one node's detail, one team's charter, or the list of teams.

kind.description: What the panel is showing: "node" one OKR node, "team" one team's charter, "teams" the list of all teams.

id.description: The node id when kind is "node", the team id when kind is "team". Absent for the teams list.

editing.description: True when the node panel is in edit mode, so the user is changing the node rather than reading it. Team panels are always editable and omit this.

field.description: The field the user's cursor is in right now, if any. "this" in a message like "what should this be?" means that field of this node or team.
